rows.quote: In the FinnGen study, the phenocodes “I9_HEARTFAIL_ALLCAUSE,” “I9_HEARTFAIL_AND_CHD,” and “I9_HEARTFAIL_AND_ANTIHYPERT” correspond to all-cause HF with 26,872 cases and 349,361 controls, HF in patients with CHD with 12,872 cases and 333,759 controls, and HF in patients receiving antihypertensive medication with 25,827 cases and 177,731 controls, respectively (Version R9).
rows.coder_note: The sentence describes the FinnGen study endpoints and writes 'Version R9' (rule A); the endpoint case and control counts are not release-defining and identify no other release (rule H).

The passages give the consortium name with exact counts (47,309 HF cases and 930,014 controls across 26 cohorts, European ancestry) and no citation, year, accession or release; exact counts with a consortium name alone do not identify a release (rules D, I1).

rows.quote: In the discovery stage, the pQTLs associated with 4,657 circulating proteins were extracted from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study, which included 7,213 individuals of European American descent [30].
rows.reference_quote: Zhang J, Dutta D, Köttgen A, Tin A, Schlosser P, Grams ME, et al. Plasma proteome analyses in individuals of European and African ancestry identify cis-pQTLs and models for proteome-wide association studies. Nat Genet. 2022;54(5):593–602. doi: 10.1038/s41588-022-01051-w.
rows.coder_note: The sentence attributes the ARIC pQTLs to reference 30 (DOI 10.1038/s41588-022-01051-w), whose source has two dictionary rows; '7,213 individuals of European American descent' in the same sentence matches the European American row only (rule E). The SomaScan platform statement elsewhere agrees.

rows.quote: In the replication stage, the pQTL associated with circulating PCSK9 was obtained from an independent large-scale pQTL study conducted in 35,559 individuals of Icelandic descent, which was part of the deCODE study [31].
rows.reference_quote: Ferkingstad E, Sulem P, Atlason BA, Sveinbjornsson G, Magnusson MI, Styrmisdottir EL, et al. Large-scale integration of the plasma proteome with genetics and disease. Nat Genet. 2021;53(12):1712–21. doi: 10.1038/s41588-021-00978-w.
rows.coder_note: The sentence attributes the replication pQTL data to reference 31 (DOI 10.1038/s41588-021-00978-w), the source of one dictionary row; 35,559 Icelandic individuals agrees with it. Reference 69 (Eldjarn 2023) is cited only for an Olink comparison, not as the dataset.
